hpi: {{patient_name}} is an older woman with hypertension on hydrochlorothiazide who presents with palpitations, syncope, dizziness, and hypotension. ECG demonstrates complete heart block (3rd degree AV block) — complete dissociation between P waves and QRS complexes with no relationship. This is a bradycardic rhythm. Third-degree AV block has an extensive differential: coronary ischemia (most common), fibrosis/sclerosis of conduction system (Lenegre/Lev disease — likely in this patient given age and HTN), Lyme disease, sarcoidosis, hyperkalemia, thyroid disorders, iatrogenic (AV nodal blockers), and congenital (unlikely — 90% symptomatic by age 30). TSH normal, troponin negative, chemistries normal, ESR normal, CBC normal — infectious and inflammatory causes unlikely. Most likely: fibrous degeneration of conduction system from aging + hypertension. Management: temporary transcutaneous/transvenous pacemaker, then permanent pacemaker placement.
